title: Open-Label Placebo Treatment for Distressed Individuals Seeking Psychotherapy.
summary:
This study investigates whether an open-label placebo (OLP) intervention can help people feel better while they are seeking outpatient psychotherapy or waiting for outpatient psychotherapy to begin. The OLPs used in this study are small, tasteless wafers made from potato starch that are taken daily like a medication but do not contain any pharmacologically active ingredients. Participants are explicitly informed that the wafers are an open-label placebo—that is, a placebo without active substances that may nevertheless have a positive effect on well-being.

The study is aimed at adults experiencing psychological distress who are actively seeking outpatient psychotherapy or waiting for outpatient psychotherapy to begin. Following telephone screening, participants are randomly assigned either to the "Group with immediate intervention start", which takes two OLPs daily for four weeks, or to the "Group with intervention start after four weeks", which receives no additional intervention during this period. After four weeks, participants in the second group may also begin the OLP intervention if they wish.

A distinctive feature of the OLP intervention examined in this study is that participants can choose one out of seven differently designed OLP options. These options are tailored to common types of psychological complaints that people frequently experience at the beginning of outpatient psychotherapy. At the start of the study and after four weeks, various aspects of mental health are assessed using online questionnaires, including psychological distress, stress, sleep quality, life satisfaction, and individually defined symptoms. In addition, treatment expectations, expected symptom improvement, and participants' perceived ability to handle challenging situations are assessed. A further follow-up assessment takes place three months after the four-week assessment.

The aim of the study is to examine whether the use of an open-label placebo while seeking outpatient psychotherapy or waiting for psychotherapy to begin has a positive effect on mood and overall well-being.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants must be at least 18 years old and actively seeking outpatient psychotherapy because of psychological distress. They must have previously contacted at least one appropriate service (e.g., a general practitioner, the German appointment service 116117, a psychotherapeutic practice, a crisis service, a community mental health service, or a telephone counselling service). Elevated psychological distress must be confirmed during telephone screening (GHQ-12 ≥ 12 using Likert scoring, total score range 0–36). At enrolment, participants must either not yet have secured a place in outpatient psychotherapy or have a psychotherapy start date no earlier than four weeks after enrolment. Sufficient proficiency in German and informed consent are required. For participants taking psychotropic medication, medication and dosage must have remained unchanged for at least two months.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are: acute suicidality; acute crisis situations requiring immediate professional assessment or treatment; acute severe psychological conditions or significant cognitive impairments preventing informed consent or appropriate study participation; ongoing outpatient, day-patient, or inpatient psychotherapy.
